extraction.Name: Lucy Shangreau
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent in fee to her 320 acre allotment when she got it, as she did not wish to have the taxes to pay on it; but she was advised by the Indian Agency that she would have to accept it, and she did so
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged her 2 section to Leedom, of Gordon, Nebraska; lost her 2 section
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she was behind in her taxes in 1922 on her allotment
extraction.Occupation/Income: supported by her husband, who receives $30.00 pension for his services as an Indian Scout, this being his only income
extraction.NOTES: Document No. 6094; mentally incompetent; health not very good, having liver trouble; husband Peter Shangreau also mortgaged a section of his allotment to Leedom of Gordon, Nebraska and lost it at the same time; they claim they were to get $2500.00 on one piece and $1200.00 on another piece, though they got only about $500.00, and never saw the money, as it was evidently turned over to Gerber by Leedom to pay for an automobile purchased from Gerber; they have a grandson to support; has never received any help from the County, State or United States Government; sworn November 22, 1928 | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 48 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal.

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
